project.name: Boardcast
project.goal: Host the agent team's blackboard as a live web app accessible remotely.

features.title: REST API for blackboard read/write
features.description: Express backend that reads and writes blackboard JSON/MD files on disk. Exposes GET /projects, GET /state/:project, PATCH /state/:project, GET /context/:project, and GET /chat/:project. Designed for file-based persistence — the filesystem is the source of truth, matching how agents already operate. Serves built React frontend as static assets from the same process so a single container is deployable.
features.rationale: Research into remote-team developer tools found that 26% of developer time is lost gathering project context across fragmented tools (2024 State of Developer Productivity). Blackboard agents already write structured JSON to disk; the pain is that there is no bridge letting a remote human read those files without SSH access. Every remote-monitoring dashboard surveyed (Grafana, Retool, Mission Control) requires a database — this API's file-first design is unique and eliminates that setup cost entirely.

features.title: Real-time blackboard sync via SSE
features.description: Server-Sent Events endpoint (GET /events?project=) that uses chokidar v4 to watch all files under BLACKBOARD_ROOT. On file change, reads the updated file and pushes a typed SSE event (snapshot | state_change | context_change | chat_message) to connected clients. Debounced at 50ms. Sets X-Accel-Buffering: no to prevent nginx proxy buffering — the single biggest production SSE failure mode identified in practitioner research.
features.rationale: Practitioners universally recommend SSE over WebSocket for server-to-client dashboards: SSE works through corporate firewalls that block WebSocket upgrades, reconnects automatically, uses ~20MB RAM for 10k connections vs ~50MB for WebSocket, and debugs with plain curl. The ~3ms latency difference is irrelevant for a blackboard dashboard where file writes happen at human speed. The X-Accel-Buffering header is critical and routinely omitted by open-source projects — Mission Control and muxplex both omit it, causing silent proxy buffering in production.

features.title: Token-based authentication with per-device revocation
features.description: Bearer token auth middleware protecting all routes and the SSE stream. Supports a TOKEN_LIST env var mapping named tokens to device labels (e.g. TOKEN_LIST=phone:abc123,laptop:def456). Tokens are passed as Authorization: Bearer <token> or ?token= query param (required since EventSource cannot set headers). Returns 401 JSON on failure. Logs auth failures with IP, timestamp, and device label.
features.rationale: Developer tool auth research shows OAuth flows are a top complaint (Jira's OAuth setup is repeatedly cited as unnecessary friction for personal tools). However, a single global token cannot be revoked per-device without rotating credentials everywhere. Named per-device tokens solve this: if a phone is lost, only that token is revoked. This is the minimal viable auth design for a personal agent-team dashboard — no user database, no OAuth server, just env-var configuration.

features.title: Human-to-agent message relay with tmux integration
features.description: POST /send endpoint accepting { project, agent, message } that writes the message to blackboard/{project}/chat.jsonl and optionally relays it into the correct tmux pane via tmux send-keys. TMUX_MAP env var (or tmux-map.json) configures agent-name → session:window:pane coordinates. Supports an ask_human answer mode: if the agent's last chat.jsonl entry is a 'question' type, the reply is formatted to match the ask_human.sh expected input. Dry-run mode for testing without a live tmux session.
features.rationale: The core gap that no existing tool solves: when an agent pauses and calls ask_human.sh, there is currently no way to answer it remotely without SSH. Linear, Jira, Notion — none of these have a concept of 'send a message to a running process'. The HN discussion on real AI agents doing work shows that human-in-the-loop escalation is the most critical reliability mechanism for production agents. This feature is Boardcast's strongest market differentiator — it is the 'remote control' that converts the dashboard from read-only observer to active supervisor.

features.title: Live blackboard kanban dashboard UI
features.description: React + Vite SPA displaying the current blackboard state: project header, features kanban grouped by status, tasks list with status badges, and a live activity feed driven by the SSE stream. Optimistic UI applies SSE patches locally immediately. Five-second-rule design: the most critical information (blocked agents, pending questions, in-progress count) visible within 5 seconds of opening. Minimal color palette (3 colors max): neutral background, one accent for active, one for blocked/danger.
features.rationale: Dashboard UX research consistently identifies information overload as the primary failure mode. The 'five-second rule' (critical data visible within 5s) is the defining principle of effective dashboards. The existing tools devs switch from (Notion/Jira) fail this test: Notion users report it is 'slow and clunky to search', Jira users report 'spending more time configuring than working'. The kanban maps directly to the blackboard's existing feature status fields — no schema translation needed, eliminating the friction that kills adoption of generic tools.

features.title: Multi-project switcher with cross-project activity feed
features.description: Sidebar listing all projects found under BLACKBOARD_ROOT (by scanning for state.json files). Clicking a project switches the dashboard context without page reload. Cross-project view shows a unified activity feed across all projects — critical when running multiple agent workstreams concurrently. Each activity item is tagged with its project name. GET /projects endpoint caches results for 5 seconds to avoid rapid disk reads.
features.rationale: Research on developer tool fragmentation (teams losing ~30% of time switching between apps) directly motivates cross-project visibility. Mission Control supports multiple projects but lacks a unified cross-project feed — developers running parallel workstreams must manually check each project. Linear's multi-team view is cited as one of its top advantages over Jira. For an agent-team orchestrator managing 3-5 concurrent projects, a unified feed showing which project is blocked or needs human input is immediately actionable.

features.title: Inline task and feature editor with status transitions
features.description: Click-to-edit on any task row — title, description, status, feature_id. Status badges are single-click state machines (pending → in_progress → done; blocked → pending). Clicking a feature card opens a drawer with full edit. All edits are sent via PATCH /state/:project with optimistic local updates that revert on API error. A '+' button creates new tasks inline with auto-generated IDs. A 'Mark blocked' button appends to a blockers[] field and immediately shows the task in the blocked column.
features.rationale: Linear's defining UX insight — 'getting out of the way' — drove their satisfaction score from 3.2/10 to 7.8/10 when teams switched from Jira. The key friction point in Jira is requiring excessive clicks and form fills for simple status updates. This feature replicates Linear's frictionless status transitions but directly on the file-based blackboard — no database migration, no webhook config, no custom field setup. Research shows this is the feature developers actually use vs. the features PM tools over-invest in.

features.title: Agent chat panel with conversation history
features.description: Split-pane chat panel showing per-agent conversation threads. Human messages (right-aligned) and agent messages (left-aligned) stored in blackboard/{project}/chat.jsonl. New messages arrive via SSE 'chat' events. Input box with agent selector dropdown targets specific agents. 'Awaiting human input' indicator fires when an agent writes a question-type entry — surfaces as a badge on the agent's thread and a notification dot on the nav. Delivery confirmation (checkmark) appears when the SSE echo arrives back.
features.rationale: The biggest blind spot in current blackboard agent systems is the absence of a persistent conversation record. ask_human.sh exchanges happen in ephemeral tmux sessions — there is no audit trail of what was asked, what was answered, or when. Research into multi-agent system debugging confirms that reconstructing the human-agent handoff chain from distributed logs is the hardest observability problem. A persistent chat log with per-agent threading solves this and creates accountability — you can see exactly what instructions were given to which agent and when.

features.title: Agent step trace and activity timeline
features.description: Per-agent timeline view showing a chronological record of file writes made by each agent: what files they touched, what status fields changed, when they started and completed tasks. Built from parsing SSE change events and attributing them to agents via the assigned_agent field in tasks. Each event is expandable to show a JSON diff of what changed. A 'time since last activity' indicator per agent surfaces stalled agents — no heartbeat in >5 minutes triggers a yellow warning, >15 minutes triggers red.
features.rationale: The #1 agent observability problem identified in 2025 research is 'catching infinite loops, circular handoffs, or stalled agents'. 89% of organizations have implemented some form of agent observability but 62% still lack step-level tracing. The existing Boardcast design had no answer to 'is my agent stuck or working?'. This feature provides the minimal viable tracing without requiring OpenTelemetry instrumentation — it derives a trace purely from filesystem changes, requiring zero changes to the agent code. This is a key differentiator vs. Langfuse/Braintrust which require SDK integration.

features.title: Context.md viewer and decisions audit log
features.description: Read-only panel rendering blackboard/{project}/context.md as formatted Markdown (via react-markdown + rehype-highlight). Re-fetches on SSE context change events. Decisions log renders the decisions[] array as a chronological timeline with timestamps, rationale, and linked feature/task ID badges. Clicking a badge highlights the corresponding kanban card. Sort newest-first. Last-updated timestamp shown on both panels.
features.rationale: Research into developer workflow complaints reveals that Notion is widely used for exactly this pattern (context + decision docs linked to tasks) but requires manual copy-paste from agent outputs. The blackboard format already mandates writing context.md and decisions[] — this feature auto-syncs them to a readable view, eliminating the 'documentation is always stale' problem that plagues Notion-based workflows. It answers the question 'why is this project in this state?' without opening files in a terminal.

features.title: Embedded web terminal for live agent session access
features.description: Optional embedded terminal panel powered by ttyd + xterm.js that provides browser-based access to the host's tmux sessions. ttyd is spawned as a sidecar process by the backend, authenticated behind the same bearer token. Terminal access is read-write but sandboxed to a specific tmux session (TERMINAL_SESSION env var). Session is recorded to a log file (optional, controlled by TERMINAL_RECORD=true). Disabled by default — enabled via TERMINAL_ENABLED=true env var.
features.rationale: Research into web terminal tooling confirms ttyd (built on libwebsockets + xterm.js) as the current state of the art — GoTTY is abandoned, muxplex uses ttyd under the hood. The muxplex project (Feb 2025) demonstrates the exact use case: viewing tmux sessions from a browser. Security research confirms the two non-negotiable requirements: authentication (no unauthenticated terminal exposure) and TLS. This feature is opt-in because it introduces WebSocket (required for bidirectional terminal I/O) alongside the SSE dashboard stream — the only place in Boardcast where WebSocket is genuinely necessary rather than SSE.

features.title: Docker single-container deployment with Railway/Fly.io config
features.description: Multi-stage Dockerfile: stage 1 builds the React SPA (vite build), stage 2 copies dist/ into the Express backend's public/ and runs the server. docker-compose.yml mounts the host blackboard directory as a volume and passes TOKEN_LIST, BLACKBOARD_ROOT, TMUX_MAP, TERMINAL_ENABLED env vars. railway.json and fly.toml configs included. GitHub Actions workflow builds and pushes on push to main, triggers a Railway/Fly.io redeploy via deploy hook. Target: under 5 minutes from fresh account to live dashboard.
features.rationale: Deployment DX research shows Railway leads on developer experience (reputation as 'best DX in the industry') while Fly.io suits globally distributed apps requiring infrastructure control. For Boardcast's target user (solo dev or small agent team), Railway's simplicity wins — connect repo, set secrets, done. The single-container approach (backend serves frontend as static assets) eliminates the orchestration overhead of separate frontend/backend services. Research on self-hosted dashboards (Grafana, Retool, Mission Control) shows multi-service setups are the #1 adoption barrier for personal tools.

tasks.title: Scaffold Express backend with TypeScript and file service
tasks.description: Initialize Node.js/Express/TypeScript project under ./boardcast/backend/. Folder structure: routes/, services/, middleware/. Environment config via dotenv (BLACKBOARD_ROOT, TOKEN_LIST, TMUX_MAP, TERMINAL_ENABLED, TERMINAL_SESSION). Create fileService.ts with resolveProjectPath(project), listProjects(), readState(project), writeState(project, patch), readContext(project), readChat(project, limit). Include GET /health endpoint. Validate BLACKBOARD_ROOT exists on startup or exit with a clear error.

tasks.title: Implement GET /projects, GET /state/:project, PATCH /state/:project
tasks.description: GET /projects scans BLACKBOARD_ROOT for subdirectories containing state.json, returns array of { id, name, status, taskCounts: { total, done, blocked } }. GET /state/:project returns full state.json. PATCH /state/:project deep-merges partial payload (arrays replaced at key level, not element level). All endpoints return 404 for unknown projects, 400 for malformed payloads, 500 with descriptive message on file errors. Log all writes with ISO timestamp.

tasks.title: Implement GET /context/:project and GET /chat/:project
tasks.description: GET /context/:project returns raw Markdown from context.md as text/plain (empty string with 200 if missing). GET /chat/:project reads chat.jsonl, parses each line as JSON, returns last N entries (default 100, configurable via ?limit= param) as JSON array sorted oldest-first. Handle missing chat.jsonl gracefully (return empty array). Include a POST /chat/:project endpoint appending a new line — used internally by POST /send and directly testable.

tasks.title: Serve React frontend as static assets from Express
tasks.description: Configure Express to serve the React build output (dist/) from a PUBLIC_DIR env var (defaults to ./public). All unmatched routes serve index.html to support React Router client-side navigation. In development, frontend runs on a separate Vite dev server with proxy config pointing /api and /events to the Express backend. In production (Docker), the built frontend is copied into the image alongside the backend.

tasks.title: Implement chokidar watcher service with event classification
tasks.description: Create WatcherService using chokidar v4 watching BLACKBOARD_ROOT recursively. On file change, classify the event: path matching */state.json → 'state_change', */context.md → 'context_change', */chat.jsonl → 'chat_message' (read last line only), other → 'file_change'. Debounce at 50ms per file path. Emit typed events internally via EventEmitter. On startup, log the watch path and inotify/kqueue backend being used.

tasks.title: Implement GET /events SSE endpoint with proxy-safe headers
tasks.description: SSE endpoint accepting ?project= filter and ?token= auth param. On connect: send Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, X-Accel-Buffering: no, Connection: keep-alive. Send an immediate 'snapshot' event with current state. Subscribe to WatcherService for project-scoped events; send as JSON SSE data. Send a heartbeat comment (:\n\n) every 15 seconds to prevent proxy timeout. On disconnect, unsubscribe to prevent memory leaks.

tasks.title: Build useSSE React hook with reconnect and patch application
tasks.description: Custom hook opening EventSource to /events?project=&token=. Handle 'snapshot' events to initialize state. Handle 'state_change' events by merging the changed fields into local state (deep merge for objects, replace for arrays at key level). Handle 'chat_message' by appending to local chat array. Implement exponential backoff reconnect (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, cap at 30s). Expose { state, chatMessages, connectionStatus: 'connected' | 'reconnecting' | 'error', lastEventAt } to consumers.

tasks.title: Implement named bearer token auth middleware
tasks.description: Middleware parsing TOKEN_LIST env var (format: 'device:token,device2:token2') into a Map<token, deviceLabel>. Checks Authorization header or ?token= query param. On success, attaches req.deviceLabel to the request. On failure, returns 401 JSON { error: 'Unauthorized' }. Logs failures with: IP, timestamp, deviceLabel (if token partially matches), and route attempted. Applies to all routes except GET /health.

tasks.title: Frontend token entry screen and persistent session
tasks.description: On first visit (no token in localStorage), show a minimal full-screen token entry form. On submit, validate against GET /health?token= — if 401, show 'Invalid token'. On success, store token in localStorage and proceed to dashboard. On all subsequent API calls and EventSource connections, include the token. On any 401 response, clear localStorage token and redirect to entry screen with a 'Session expired' message. Include a logout button in the nav.

tasks.title: Implement POST /send endpoint with chat.jsonl write
tasks.description: Accept { project, agent, message, type: 'reply' | 'instruction' } (type defaults to 'instruction'). Validate: project exists, agent is non-empty string, message is non-empty string (max 2000 chars). Write to blackboard/{project}/chat.jsonl as JSONL: { ts: ISO, from: 'human', agent, message, type }. Return { ok: true, ts }. The WatcherService detects the chat.jsonl change and broadcasts the new line to SSE clients.

tasks.title: Implement tmux relay service and answer-injection for ask_human
tasks.description: TmuxService parses TMUX_MAP env var (format: 'agent:session:window:pane,...') into agent-to-pane map. sendToAgent(agent, message) runs: tmux send-keys -t session:window.pane 'message' Enter via child_process.execFile (not exec — no shell injection). If TMUX_RELAY env var is false or pane is not found, log a warning but still write to chat.jsonl. Include a isSessionAlive(agent) check method. Dry-run mode logs the command without executing.

tasks.title: Frontend message input with agent selector and question badge
tasks.description: In the chat panel, a bottom input bar with: agent selector dropdown (populated from state.tasks' distinct assigned_agent values), text input, send button. Disable send while empty or while previous request is in-flight. Show a 'Awaiting your reply' badge on agent thread headers when the latest chat entry has type='question'. Clicking the badge focuses the input with that agent pre-selected.

tasks.title: Build project header and features kanban board
tasks.description: Project header showing: name, goal, status badge, task completion fraction (X/Y done). Kanban board with columns for each feature status (pending, in_progress, done, blocked). Feature cards show: title, priority badge, task count, and a micro progress bar (done/total tasks). Cards are drag-and-drop reorderable within columns (updates feature.status via PATCH). Blocked column is visually distinct (red left border). Data purely from useSSE state — no separate fetch.

tasks.title: Build task list with status badges and live activity feed
tasks.description: Task list below kanban showing all tasks for selected feature (or all tasks if none selected). Columns: ID, title, status badge (color-coded), assigned_agent. Filter bar for status and feature_id. Activity feed sidebar showing last 50 SSE events as human-readable strings ('Task T04 moved to done', 'Feature F02 updated description'). Auto-scrolls to latest. Relative timestamps ('2s ago'). New events pulse briefly on arrival.

tasks.title: Backend project scan and frontend project switcher
tasks.description: GET /projects returns array of { id, name, status, taskCounts } cached for 5 seconds. Frontend sidebar lists all projects, refreshes every 30 seconds. Clicking a project sets selectedProject in a React context (persisted in localStorage). All dashboard components subscribe to selectedProject and re-render. Unread activity indicator (dot) on each project showing unread SSE events since last visit. Cross-project 'All Projects' view shows unified activity feed tagged by project.

tasks.title: Cross-project summary view with blocked-items aggregation
tasks.description: An 'All Projects' overview panel (accessible from the project switcher) showing a summary card per project: name, status, in-progress count, blocked count (red badge if >0), last activity time. Blocked items across all projects are aggregated into a 'Needs Attention' section at the top — tasks with status='blocked' and agents with pending questions. This view is the default landing page if >1 project exists.

tasks.title: Inline status toggle and task detail drawer
tasks.description: Clicking a task's status badge cycles through valid transitions using a predefined state machine (pending→in_progress, in_progress→done, done→pending, blocked→pending). Sends PATCH /state/:project with { tasks: [{ id, status }] }. Optimistic update reverts on error with toast. Clicking a task row opens a side drawer with: editable title/description (on-blur save), status selector, feature_id dropdown, 'Mark blocked' button (prompts for reason, sets status='blocked', appends to blockers[]).

tasks.title: New task and feature creation forms
tasks.description: A '+' button at the bottom of the task list opens an inline form: title (required, max 200 chars), feature_id (dropdown), description (optional textarea). Auto-generates ID as T{maxExistingN+1}. Submits via PATCH /state/:project appending to tasks[]. A separate '+' button on the kanban creates new features similarly (F{maxN+1}). Auto-closes and scrolls to the new item. Shows validation errors inline (not toast) to avoid missing them.

tasks.title: Backend chat.jsonl read, write, SSE integration, and ask_human detection
tasks.description: Extend fileService with appendChat(project, entry). Extend WatcherService to watch *.jsonl files: on change, read the last line, parse as JSON, emit 'chat_message' SSE event with { project, entry }. Add GET /chat/:project endpoint. Detect ask_human pattern: if entry.from !== 'human' AND entry.type === 'question' (or message contains '?'), mark as awaitingReply: true in the SSE event. This allows frontend to surface the 'Awaiting reply' badge without any agent code changes.

tasks.title: Agent chat panel UI with threaded view and delivery confirmation
tasks.description: Chat panel with agent tabs (one tab per distinct agent seen in chat history). Each tab shows a message thread: human messages right-aligned (blue), agent messages left-aligned (gray). Timestamps on hover. 'Awaiting your reply' banner at top of thread when awaitingReply=true. Input at bottom with send button. Delivery confirmation: message shows clock icon until SSE echo arrives, then checkmark. 'No messages yet' empty state per agent.

tasks.title: Implement agent step trace timeline from SSE event log
tasks.description: Maintain an in-memory event log per agent by attributing SSE state_change events to agents via the task's assigned_agent field. WatcherService emits agent attribution metadata when a task's status changes. Frontend renders per-agent timeline: each entry shows timestamp, event type ('Task T04: pending→in_progress'), and a JSON diff toggle. A 'last active' timestamp per agent with color coding: green (<5m), yellow (5-15m), red (>15m stalled).

tasks.title: Stalled agent detection and notification badge
tasks.description: WatcherService tracks lastActivityAt per agent (updated whenever a state_change event is attributed to that agent). A GET /agents/:project endpoint returns { agentName, lastActivityAt, stalledMinutes, status: 'active'|'idle'|'stalled' } array. Frontend polls this endpoint every 60 seconds (not SSE — polling is fine for minute-granularity status). Stalled agents (>15m no activity) show a red badge in the sidebar. Clicking navigates to the agent's trace timeline.

tasks.title: Context.md Markdown viewer with live sync
tasks.description: Panel fetching GET /context/:project on mount and re-fetching on SSE 'context_change' events. Renders Markdown via react-markdown with rehype-highlight for code blocks and remark-gfm for tables. Shows 'Last updated: X minutes ago' timestamp using the file modification time returned by a HEAD /context/:project response (Last-Modified header). Falls back to a 'No context file found' placeholder. Read-only — no editing.

tasks.title: Decisions audit log timeline component
tasks.description: Read decisions[] from useSSE state and render as a vertical timeline list sorted newest-first. Each entry: ISO timestamp (formatted as relative), decision summary, rationale field (collapsible), feature_id and task_id as clickable badges that highlight the corresponding kanban card by adding a pulsing ring CSS animation for 3 seconds. Empty state: 'No decisions logged yet — agents write here via the decisions[] array.' Newest entry is highlighted on first render.

tasks.title: Backend ttyd sidecar spawner and terminal session config
tasks.description: If TERMINAL_ENABLED=true, spawn ttyd as a child process on a random ephemeral port (stored in process memory). ttyd is configured with: --credential (same token as API auth), --writable, tmux attach-session -t TERMINAL_SESSION. Proxy /terminal WebSocket traffic from Express to the ttyd port using http-proxy-middleware. On backend shutdown, kill the ttyd child process. Log ttyd startup errors clearly. If ttyd binary not found in PATH, log a warning and disable terminal silently.

tasks.title: Frontend embedded terminal panel with xterm.js
tasks.description: An optional 'Terminal' tab in the dashboard (hidden unless TERMINAL_ENABLED is returned as true by a GET /config endpoint). Tab opens an xterm.js instance connecting to /terminal WebSocket. Terminal is full-height within its panel. Includes a 'Detach' button (sends Ctrl+B D to tmux). Security note: displayed in UI — 'This terminal has full shell access. Handle with care.' Token is passed in the WebSocket URL query param for authentication.

tasks.title: Multi-stage Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml
tasks.description: Stage 1 (node:20-alpine): COPY frontend/, run npm ci && vite build, output to /app/dist. Stage 2 (node:20-alpine): COPY backend/, COPY --from=stage1 /app/dist ./public, run npm ci --omit=dev, CMD node dist/server.js. Exposed port: 3000. docker-compose.yml: service boardcast, image build from Dockerfile, volumes: [./blackboard:/blackboard:ro] (read-only mount), env_file: .env. .dockerignore excludes node_modules, .git, *.log. Include a docker-compose.dev.yml for local development with hot reload.

tasks.title: Railway and Fly.io deployment configs with one-command setup
tasks.description: railway.json: { "$schema": "https://railway.app/railway.schema.json", "build": { "builder": "DOCKERFILE" }, "deploy": { "healthcheckPath": "/health", "restartPolicyType": "ON_FAILURE" } }. fly.toml: app name, region, internal port 3000, health check on /health, persistent volume for blackboard at /blackboard. scripts/deploy-railway.sh: one-command deploy. scripts/deploy-fly.sh: fly launch + fly volumes create + fly deploy. README section: exact commands for first deploy, estimated time: under 5 minutes.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline
tasks.description: Workflow .github/workflows/deploy.yml triggering on push to main. Steps: checkout, setup-node, npm ci (backend + frontend), tsc --noEmit type check, vite build (frontend), docker build + push to GHCR (ghcr.io/{owner}/{repo}:latest). Secrets: GHCR_TOKEN, RAILWAY_TOKEN (or FLY_API_TOKEN). Final step: POST to Railway/Fly.io deploy hook URL (stored as secret DEPLOY_HOOK_URL) to trigger redeploy. Includes a manual workflow_dispatch trigger for one-click redeploys from GitHub UI.
